novel_features.name: Fleet firmware status
novel_features.description: Check every model in your installed fleet against current firmware in one command.
novel_features.rationale: Firmware releases are family-scoped, so one release governs many models; resolving that many-to-many mapping requires a local series-to-model join that no single page provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of checking models one at a time; it also catches releases that a per-model search would miss because the release is titled under a sibling model.

novel_features.name: Release-note full-text search
novel_features.description: Search every firmware release note and change log at once for a term.
novel_features.rationale: Release notes live on login-gated per-version pages and have never been searchable across versions anywhere.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'which version fixed X' without opening a dozen version pages.

novel_features.name: Release-note diff
novel_features.description: Show what changed between two firmware versions for a model.
novel_features.rationale: Change logs exist only as separate per-version HTML pages with no diff view on the site.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when deciding whether an upgrade is worth scheduling on a live site.

novel_features.name: Submittal package builder
novel_features.description: Download every documentation asset for a list of models into per-model folders with a coverage report.
novel_features.rationale: The per-product resource endpoint returns roughly twenty assets spanning CAD, Revit, CSI Guide Specs, Security Reference Guides, manuals and spec sheets; nothing on the site fans that out over a model list.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to assemble a CSI submittal package in one step instead of hundreds of individual downloads.

novel_features.name: Lifecycle and replacement trace
novel_features.description: Report whether a model is still sellable and trace its replacement chain.
novel_features.rationale: An unadvertised replacement-products endpoint plus the dated End-of-Sale notice stream let the successor chain be walked transitively and in bulk.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when triaging an as-built list to find which parts can still be ordered and what replaced the rest.

novel_features.name: Spec table comparison
novel_features.description: Compare two models field by field across the full specification table.
novel_features.rationale: The parsed specification table is stored locally, so two products can be aligned by section and key; the website renders one product at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when choosing between sibling models in the same series, which often differ in only a few spec rows.

narrative.headline: Every Crestron product, spec sheet, and firmware release — searchable offline, with fleet-wide currency checks the website cannot do.
narrative.value_prop: Crestron.com has no public API and no way to ask a question across more than one product at a time. This CLI mirrors the product catalog, the documentation library, and the firmware release history into local SQLite, then answers the questions integrators actually have: what firmware covers my installed models, what changed between two versions, which parts are discontinued and what replaced them. Sign in and it also unlocks release notes and firmware downloads.
narrative.auth_narrative: Most of this CLI works with no account at all: the product catalog, specifications, spec sheets, manuals, certificates, CAD and Revit files, and firmware version numbers and release dates are all public. A Crestron account unlocks two more things — firmware release notes and the firmware binaries themselves. Run `crestron-pp-cli auth login --chrome` and the CLI imports your existing Crestron.com session cookies straight from Chrome; it never asks for or stores your password.

quickstart.comment: confirm the CLI can reach Crestron.com before syncing anything
build the local catalog mirror; this is what makes offline search possible
look up a model by number to confirm the mirror is populated
read the full specification table as structured output
check whether a part is still sellable and what replaced it

troubleshoots.symptom: Firmware release notes come back empty or a download redirects to a sign-in page
troubleshoots.fix: Run `crestron-pp-cli auth login --chrome` — release notes and binaries require a Crestron account session.

troubleshoots.symptom: `fleet status` reports a model as unknown
troubleshoots.fix: Run `crestron-pp-cli sync --resources products,releases` so the series-to-model mapping is populated.

troubleshoots.symptom: Local results look out of date
troubleshoots.fix: Run `crestron-pp-cli sync` again to refresh the local mirror; re-running is always safe.

troubleshoots.symptom: A search returns nothing for a model you know exists
troubleshoots.fix: Crestron groups firmware by family, so search the series instead, or use `crestron-pp-cli fleet status` which resolves the mapping for you.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for any question about Crestron hardware that lives on Crestron.com rather than on a device: what a product is, what its specifications are, which firmware version is current, what changed in a release, which documentation exists for a model, and whether a part has been discontinued. It is especially strong for questions spanning many models at once, which the website cannot answer at all.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to control, configure, or communicate with Crestron hardware on a network — it never talks to devices. Use Crestron Toolbox or the Crestron EDK PowerShell modules for that.
Do not use this CLI to push or install firmware onto a control processor or touch panel; it only downloads the files.
Do not use this CLI for Crestron Home smart-home control such as lights, shades, or scenes.
Do not use this CLI to obtain dealer pricing — Crestron's public pricing endpoint returns no data for most models.
